title: The Matador Meeting
summary: White House record of a 19 March 1975 meeting, held the day The New York Times ran Seymour Hersh's story on the Glomar Explorer, in which President Ford, Defense Secretary Schlesinger and CIA Director Colby discuss whether to confirm the submarine operation. Schlesinger calls it 'a marvel' and urges admitting the bare facts, but Colby's advice to stay silent prevailed.

tree.title: Memorandum of conversation: Matador meeting
tree.summary: Secret/NODIS White House record of a Wednesday, March 19, 1975, 11:20 a.m. Cabinet Room meeting of President Ford, Schlesinger, Buchen, Marsh, Rumsfeld, Scowcroft and CIA Director Colby. Schlesinger calls the operation a marvel and urges acknowledging the bare facts, since "no comment" will be read as confirmation. Colby, recalling the U-2, warns against pressuring the Soviets to respond.

nodes.title: Participants and Schlesinger's case for going public
nodes.summary: Participants, time and place, then the talk: Schlesinger calls the episode a major American accomplishment, a marvel technically and in secrecy. With no plausible denial story, he urges acknowledging the bare facts to take the high ground, offering to announce it himself as a Navy role too. Marsh asks who would put it out; Ford asks Colby's view.

nodes.title: Colby's reply and the Soviet reaction
nodes.summary: Page 2: Colby goes back to the U-2 affair and says the Soviet Union should not be put under such pressure to respond. Ford notes that CBS reported from Moscow there was no official comment, but that the Soviets were aware.

tree.summary: NARA withdrawal sheet, ID 017986: Brent Scowcroft's one-page notes for this memcon, dated 03/19/1975, are withheld under a national security restriction.
